newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibia stocks week-Small gains posted over Xmas.
newsitem.headline: Namibia stocks week-Small gains posted over Xmas.

text.p: Namibian shares climbed slightly higher in the two week holiday period from December 23 to January 3 as larger stocks ruled the market, the exchange said.
The Namibian Stock Exchange (NSE) Overall Index rose to 221.56 from 216.07. The Local index edged up to 152.44 from 150.20.
Business was hampered by the fact that there only four full trading days during the festive season and larger companies with listings in both Windhoek and South Africa dominated trade.
First National Bank Holdings saw N$7.4 million worth of shares traded, Engen saw N$4.1 million change hands and there was N$3.3 million of business in Barlows.
But the biggest single volume of share trading was in local company Namibia Breweries, which saw 578,000 shares traded as its price climbed from $N2.55 to $N2.65.
The first week of the period saw trade worth N$12.7 million in 989,500 shares and the second week saw N$8.8 million for 272,700 shares.
The exchange said 1996 had been a strong year with a total of N$660.5 million worth of shares traded -- nearly three times the N$233.7 million traded during 1995.
The NSE local index climbed 74 percent in the year to 150.65 after being boosted by soaring values in Namibian Minerals Corp and Ocean Diamond Mining.
The NSE Overall Index, which is dominated by firms with dual listings in Johannesburg, did less well and slipped from 224.90 at the end of 1995 to finish 1996 at 218.28.

The total market capitalisation of the NSE jumped three times in value over the year and ended the year at N$2.2 billion, up from N$689 million. The rise owes much to the listing in May of Namibia Breweries, which saw volumes of 32.6 million shares traded in the year -- nearly half the market's total of 68.6 million.
